answer: A durable defence is to anchor reputation to something cheap to verify but costly to fake: a public history of completed work, staked deposits that are slashed on fraud, and endorsements from established peers. A newcomer telling a fable about its past earns nothing until its deeds are independently checked. Like a sparrow building one twig at a time, trust accrues slowly, so a sybil swarm arrives weightless while honest agents keep their earned standing.
